name: Silphium

study_strategy.warning: Central Texas Silphium names have shifted. Old S. integrifolium var. asperrimum and var. radulum labels should not be reassigned automatically under modern species concepts.

quick_split: S. albiflorum — white ray flowers + rough often deeply divided leaves; project PASS (Travis, Burnet, Mason).
S. radula — broad rough/scabrous leaves and stems + yellow heads; project PASS (Hays, Williamson, Kerr).
S. laciniatum — huge deeply pinnatifid compass leaves + yellow heads; project RANGE HOLD because known Hays occurrence is introduced.
S. integrifolium — broad entire leaves + yellow heads; taxonomy/range HOLD because historical Central Texas varietal names do not map cleanly to current species concepts.

look_here_first: First photograph the WHOLE basal and stem leaves, not only the sunflower-like flower head. WHITE rays strongly indicate S. albiflorum among these three. For YELLOW heads, broad rough undivided sessile leaves suggest S. radula, while very large deeply divided (pinnatifid) lower leaves suggest the range-unresolved S. laciniatum. Then photograph a head from the side to show the PHYLARIES (involucral bracts) below its ray/disk florets. Separate plant identification from target-county nativity.

shared_traits: Coarse perennial herbs with often resinous and harshly hairy foliage.
Sunflower-like composite HEADS containing outer RAY FLORETS and central DISK FLORETS.
PHYLARIES form the involucre beneath each head; inspect their shape and orientation in side view.
Fruit is a dry CYPSELA (aster-family fruit); in Silphium, outer fertile ray florets produce the principal cypselae.
shared_genus_pattern.glossary: PINNATIFID = deeply lobed along a central blade axis but lobes remain connected; SESSILE = leaf without a distinct stalk; SCABROUS = sandpapery rough; PHYLARY = modified bract below a flower head; RAY FLORET = strap-like outer floret; DISK FLORET = tiny central floret.
shared_genus_pattern.caution: White/yellow ray color routes these three, not every Silphium on Earth. Old varietal names and hybrid/intermediate material require scientific review.

field_key: 1. Check RAY color on a flowering head: white → S. albiflorum, confirm with coarse often pinnately lobed leaves.
2. Yellow rays → examine FULL LOWER LEAF, not just the flowering top.
3. Broad rough, mainly undivided sessile leaves and heads near leafy stems → S. radula (subject to taxonomic look-alikes).
4. Very large deeply divided lower leaves and tall comparatively leafless flowering stalk → S. laciniatum comparison only; project county status remains RANGE_UNRESOLVED.
5. Ambiguous yellow-headed specimen with neither confident leaf pattern → Silphium sp.; check S. integrifolium and close relatives; no forced ID.
